source_title: IOC Olympic host requirements and post-Games venue evidence
unit_or_scope: Olympic host cities and 982 permanent venues across 53 Games
direct_observation: Hosts must align sustainability and legacy with long-term plans; IOC reports 86% of permanent venues overall and 94% since 2000 remain in use
closed_stage: legacy requirement and aggregate venue use
missing_stage: neighbourhood equity affordability maintenance access and local meaning
evidence_status: high for institutional evidence; medium for outcomes
next_test: match one venue to post-event users budget and access

unit_or_scope: host-city residents informal settlements vendors and homeless people
direct_observation: Mega-events can drive development-induced displacement through construction clearance beautification speculation and changed housing costs
missing_stage: named household livelihood restoration return and remedy
evidence_status: high for mechanism; medium for named outcomes
next_test: follow one host neighbourhood before during and after event

source_title: OECD Paris 2024 legacy jobs procurement and SMEs
unit_or_scope: Paris 2024 host economy and local firms/workers
direct_observation: Strategic procurement social clauses training apprenticeships and SME opportunities can extend local development beyond an event
missing_stage: contract receipt payment skill retention and post-event work
evidence_status: high for mechanism; medium for effects
next_test: link named supplier and worker to contract and later employment

source_title: IOC future-host Olympic village housing requirements
unit_or_scope: Olympic villages and host housing strategies
direct_observation: Host proposals must explain future ownership housing types financing and fit with long-term housing strategy
missing_stage: affordable allocation resident continuity services and displacement
evidence_status: high for formal requirement; medium for delivery
next_test: trace one village from land to post-Games tenancy

source_title: UN Using Mega Sporting Events to create a lasting legacy
unit_or_scope: global mega-sporting-event rights and legacy examples
direct_observation: Events can create gender minority-business migrant-rights and inclusion opportunities while carrying worker displacement expression and protest risks
missing_stage: named event worker/resident remedy and reputation after scrutiny
evidence_status: high for risk/opportunity; medium for closure
next_test: build rights and legacy ledger for one event corridor

source_title: OECD Legacy of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games
unit_or_scope: Paris 2024 SOLIDEO procurement and Games-related construction workforce
direct_observation: EUR 4.4 billion procurement plan awarded 37 percent or EUR 826 million to local MSMEs and social-economy entities; 23.5 percent of construction hours were performed by people on integration pathways and 90 percent of suppliers were based in France
missing_stage: firm survival worker pay and retention post-event work resident benefit housing and cultural belonging
evidence_status: official OECD assessment; target and award evidence without long-term worker or firm follow-up
next_test: trace named suppliers and workers through payment skills retention post-event work and local resident outcomes

source_title: Paris 2024 village and venue legacy documentation
unit_or_scope: Olympic and Media Village sites and public venues in Seine-Saint-Denis
direct_observation: Documentation reports nearly 4000 homes across village sites; Olympic Village planned about 2800 homes for approximately 6000 residents with schools childcare and green space; permanent facilities were intended for local residents and venues reopened publicly
closed_stage: designed and partially operating housing venue and neighbourhood legacy
missing_stage: affordability allocation displaced-household access maintenance repeat use low-income access and belonging
evidence_status: official Paris 2024 and IOC accounts; asset and reopening evidence without distributional longitudinal outcomes
next_test: follow named neighbourhood housing allocation venue users maintenance budgets and resident wellbeing for two post-event periods

source_title: UK Government Birmingham 2022 one-year post-Games evaluation
unit_or_scope: Birmingham West Midlands and UK Games and legacy programmes through August 2023
direct_observation: Independent mixed-method evaluation uses contribution analysis and assesses outcomes one year after the Games while explicitly excluding longer-term impacts not yet realised
closed_stage: credible short-term evaluation and explicit time/attribution boundary
missing_stage: long-run housing employment wellbeing maintenance displacement trust and geopolitical reputation
evidence_status: official government evaluation; one-year scope and contribution analysis do not establish durable legacy
next_test: repeat measurement at two and five years with same places workers residents and facilities
